standard_prerequisites.name: Countable Borel equivalence relations and their graph decompositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: A CBER E on a standard Borel space X has countable classes, so E is the union of the graphs of Borel involutions, and an increasing sequence of bounded-degree Borel graphs G_n with union E is the standard decomposition used throughout the article. Borel hyperfiniteness of a restriction E restricted to a Borel set means a Borel reduction of that restriction to eventual equality.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both the statement and the proof start from such a decomposition; no hyperfiniteness of E itself is assumed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Graph distance and k-separated sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a graph G and a set B of vertices, B is k-separated when any two distinct points of B have G-distance greater than k; the article's own definition is retained from source lines 419-421.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis that each B_n is f(n)-separated in G_n is what bounds the diameter of the components built in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary graph metric estimates
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a shortest path between two vertices leaves a set and the intermediate vertices lie in one connected component of a fixed subgraph, the triangle inequality bounds the distance between the endpoints by the diameter of that component plus the two entering edges.
standard_prerequisites.use: Used inside the Claim at source line 602 to obtain dist_{G_{n+1}}(x,x') <= f(n)+2.

core_obligations: Define the increasing sequence H_0 contained in H_1 contained in ... contained in E by H_0 empty and H_{n+1} = H_n union the G_{n+1}-edges inside B meeting B_{n+1}, and verify that the union of the H_n restricted to B equals E restricted to B, using that each G_n-edge inside B has an endpoint in some B_k with k at least n (source lines 591-595).

Prove the inner Claim, by induction on n, that every connected component of H_n has diameter at most f(n): argue that a component of H_{n+1} contains at most one point of B_{n+1}, since a shortest path between two such points has its interior in one H_n-component, giving dist_{G_{n+1}}(x,x') <= f(n)+2 <= f(n+1) against the f(n+1)-separation of B_{n+1} (source line 602).

Having shown a component H of H_{n+1} meets B_{n+1} in at most one point x, describe its vertex set as the union of the H_n-components adjacent to x through G_{n+1} and deduce diam(H) <= 2(f(n)+1) <= f(n+1) (source lines 604-605).
Conclude from H_n contained in G_n, which has bounded degrees, that each H_n has finite components of uniformly bounded diameter, hence that E restricted to B is hyperfinite (source line 608).
Check that the growth hypothesis f(n+1) >= 2(f(n)+1) is used at exactly the two places where the factor 2 and the offset 1 appear, so that no weaker growth assumption can be substituted silently.

proof_roadmap.step: Build the increasing sequence H_n from the G_n and the separated sets B_n, and check that its union restricted to B is all of E restricted to B.
Prove the Claim by induction on n: a component of H_{n+1} has at most one point of B_{n+1}, and then its diameter is at most twice (f(n)+1).
Combine bounded degrees of G_n with the diameter bound to obtain hyperfiniteness of E restricted to B.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Theorem t:separation2 at source lines 425-430: an increasing sequence of bounded-degree Borel graphs G_n covering a CBER E, a scale f with f(n+1) >= 2(f(n)+1), and Borel sets B_n that are f(n)-separated in G_n jointly force E restricted to B, where B is the set of points lying in infinitely many B_n, to be hyperfinite. The construction H_{n+1} = H_n union the G_{n+1}-edges inside B meeting B_{n+1} (source line 593) is one line, but the diameter bound is not: the inner Claim at lines 597-606 first has to exclude two points of B_{n+1} in one component of H_{n+1} by routing the interior of a shortest path through a single component of H_n and applying the induction hypothesis, which yields dist_{G_{n+1}}(x,x') <= f(n)+2 <= f(n+1) against the separation of B_{n+1} (line 602). The remaining vertices are then one H_n-component per G_{n+1}-neighbour of the single B_{n+1}-point, giving diam(H) <= 2(f(n)+1) <= f(n+1) (lines 604-605). The factor 2 with the +1 offset is what makes this induction close, so neither a bounded-degree counting argument alone nor a direct matching decomposition of E restricted to B reaches the conclusion.

dedup.scope: Same-source public primary and the claim already prepared from this source, plus the public identity index, the retired-claims record and the current worklist searched with the object names separated set, bounded degree Borel graph, hyperfinite, sufficiently separated cover, topological Ramsey space and comeager.

compared.difference: Same source, different proposition: l:indep2 (source lines 540-550) starts from one bounded-degree Borel graph on the Ellentuck space and finds a cone [A'] on which the graph is contained in eventual equality. There is no sequence of graphs, no separated family B_n and no hyperfiniteness conclusion.

Counts the article's main theorem t:ramsey hyperfin (source lines 412-414, restated at 645-647), which is obtained by applying the present theorem to the separated covers built in Lemma ramsey separation. The present statement is therefore upstream of that one and is not one of its corollaries; the two have different hypotheses (a bounded-degree decomposition plus separated Borel sets versus a topological Ramsey space) and different objects.

editorial_notes: The counted statement is the introduction's Theorem t:separation2 (source lines 425-430). Its proof is not the adjacent environment: the author restates the same theorem as a namedthm* at source line 582 and proves it at 589-609, so the restatement is retained as context and makes the pairing visible; the pairing is by the author's own reference to the label t:separation2, not by proximity.

The retained section and theorem counters restore the article's numbering, so the retained definition prints as Definition 1.3 and the counted theorem as Theorem 1.4, exactly as in the source. The Claim carried inside the proof is renumbered because the article's section headings are not reproduced.
The footnote in the theorem statement, that graphs are not assumed irreflexive throughout the paper, is part of the author's statement and is retained verbatim.
No retained line contains a citation, a figure or an included file, so the package declares neither a bibliography nor an asset.

editorial_scope: One original result: the article's Theorem t:separation2 with its complete author proof, together with the author's own definition of a k-separated set. The article's main theorem t:ramsey hyperfin, the earlier Lemma l:indep2 and the generic-hyperfiniteness theorem of Subsection 3.3 are not counted here and are not used as premises.
